focus: Masculine completed past giving versus female and plural examples
englishPrompt: He gave food to the boy.

comparisons.english: She gave food to the boy.
They gave food to the boy.

attestedObservations: Lesson 14 maps He to Team deout khean laedkas in this past giving context.
Both English he and she examples begin Team, while the they example starts Teamov.
The he example uses deout, the she example deut, and the they example deout. This is observed, not yet a generalized past verb conjugation rule.
The recipient expressions are distinct written forms laedkas (he), ladkaess (she), and laedkaess (they). The grammatical status of their spellings and case forms remains unconfirmed.
All three share subject + giving form + khean + recipient ordering. The two spaces after deout in the Lesson 13 original are preserved in that record.
uncertain: Whether the giving verb and recipient form changes are controlled by subject gender or number, object/recipient agreement, context, or Romanization conventions.

Whether laedkas, ladkaess, and laedkaess represent different case endings or spelling variants.
